<!--
STEP 1 OF 2 (QC). Next: scrnaseq_2_ClusterCalling.Rmd.

What this does, per sample:
  1. Load the CellBender-filtered .h5 (ambient RNA removed, empty droplets already dropped).
  2. Optionally fix feature IDs so they match your annotation tables.
  3. Plot nFeature / nCount / log10GenesPerUMI (and percent_mito if you have mitochondrial genes).
  4. Filter on nFeature / nCount (and percent_mito).
  5. Detect doublets with scDblFinder ON THE FILTERED CELLS (see the note in that chunk), drop them.
  6. Save one filtered .rds per sample + a QC summary table.

Fill in every "<fill in: ...>" in the Configuration chunk. The first chunk after it stops if any
are left. Set thresholds AFTER looking at the pre-filter plots: the defaults are the values used
for Pocillopora damicornis, not universal numbers.
-->

# Setup

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE)
```

```{r libraries}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(Seurat)
library(scCustomize)        # Read_CellBender_h5_Mat()
library(scDblFinder)        # BiocManager::install(c("scDblFinder", "SingleCellExperiment"))
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(conflicted)

conflicts_prefer(
  dplyr::select, dplyr::filter, dplyr::count, dplyr::rename,
  base::intersect, base::union, base::setdiff,
  .quiet = TRUE
)
```

# Configuration

```{r config}
SPECIES <- "<fill in: species code, e.g. Pdam>"

# Folder with the CellBender *_filtered.h5 files, and where QC outputs should go
# (paths are relative to the project root found by here::here()).
cellbender_dir <- here("<fill in: folder with CellBender .h5 files, e.g. cellbender_output/Pdam>")
qc_out_dir     <- here("<fill in: output folder, e.g. output/Pdam/QC>")

# One row per sample. `covariate` is whatever distinguishes samples biologically or technically
# (genotype, treatment, batch...); it is carried into the clustering step to check mixing.
sample_config <- tribble(
  ~sample_id,                           ~covariate,                          ~file,
  "<fill in: sample ID 1>",             "<fill in: e.g. genotype 1>",        "<fill in: sample1_cellbender_output_filtered.h5>",
  "<fill in: sample ID 2>",             "<fill in: e.g. genotype 2>",        "<fill in: sample2_cellbender_output_filtered.h5>"
)
COVARIATE_NAME <- "genotype"   # what the covariate column means (used in plot labels)

# Optional: make feature IDs match your annotation tables. GeneExt/CellBender IDs for Pdam use
# underscores (pdam_00025168) while downstream tables use dashes (pdam-00025168).
# Use identity (function(x) x) to leave IDs unchanged.
fix_feature_ids <- function(x) gsub("_", "-", x)

# Optional mitochondrial filter. NULL = no mito genes in your reference (true for Pdam and Gfas).
# Otherwise a regex matching mitochondrial gene IDs (e.g. "^mt-") or a character vector of IDs.
MITO_GENES <- NULL
max_percent_mito <- 20   # only used when MITO_GENES is set

# QC thresholds -- check them against the pre-filter plots below before trusting them.
# Defaults = values used for P. damicornis (cross-checked against Cole et al. 2024 and
# Valadez-Ingersoll et al. 2025 for other cnidarians).
qcMetricsThresholds <- c(
  "min_nFeature_RNA" = 300,
  "max_nFeature_RNA" = 6000,
  "min_nCount_RNA"   = 400,
  "max_nCount_RNA"   = 35000
)
noveltyReferenceThreshold <- 0.80   # log10GenesPerUMI reference line: plotted, NOT used to filter

SEED <- 20260827
```

```{r check-config}
cfg_values <- c(SPECIES, cellbender_dir, qc_out_dir, unlist(sample_config))
stopifnot("Replace every '<fill in: ...>' value in the Configuration chunk first." =
            !any(grepl("<fill in", cfg_values, fixed = TRUE)))

sample_config <- sample_config %>% mutate(path = file.path(cellbender_dir, file))
stopifnot("One or more CellBender .h5 files not found -- check cellbender_dir and file names." =
            all(file.exists(sample_config$path)))
stopifnot("sample_id values must be unique." = !anyDuplicated(sample_config$sample_id))

qc_rds_dir <- file.path(qc_out_dir, "QC_Files")
dir.create(qc_rds_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

qcMetrics.tmp <- c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "log10GenesPerUMI",
                   if (!is.null(MITO_GENES)) "percent_mito")
sample_config
```

# Load CellBender-filtered counts

```{r load-objects}
# CellBender already removed empty droplets, so no separate emptyDrops() step.
sample.list <- pmap(sample_config, function(sample_id, covariate, file, path) {
  message("Loading ", sample_id, " ...")
  mat <- Read_CellBender_h5_Mat(path)
  rownames(mat) <- fix_feature_ids(rownames(mat))
  obj <- CreateSeuratObject(mat)

  obj$sample_id <- sample_id
  obj$covariate <- covariate

  # Complexity/novelty score: mito-independent sign of damaged / low-complexity droplets.
  obj$log10GenesPerUMI <- log10(obj$nFeature_RNA) / log10(obj$nCount_RNA)

  if (!is.null(MITO_GENES)) {
    if (length(MITO_GENES) == 1) {
      obj$percent_mito <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = MITO_GENES)
    } else {
      obj$percent_mito <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, features = intersect(MITO_GENES, rownames(obj)))
    }
  }
  obj
})
names(sample.list) <- sample_config$sample_id

map_int(sample.list, ncol)
```

# QC diagnostic plots (pre-filter)

```{r qc-plots}
walk2(sample.list, names(sample.list), function(obj, sid) {
  plot_df <- obj@meta.data %>%
    select(all_of(qcMetrics.tmp)) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = qcMetrics.tmp))

  thresh_df <- tibble(
    metric    = str_replace(names(qcMetricsThresholds), "^(min|max)_", ""),
    threshold = unname(qcMetricsThresholds)
  ) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(metric = "log10GenesPerUMI", threshold = noveltyReferenceThreshold)) %>%
    bind_rows(if (!is.null(MITO_GENES)) tibble(metric = "percent_mito", threshold = max_percent_mito)) %>%
    filter(metric %in% qcMetrics.tmp) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = qcMetrics.tmp))

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = "sample", y = value)) +
    geom_violin() +
    ggrastr::rasterise(geom_jitter(size = 0.5), dpi = 300) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = length(qcMetrics.tmp), scales = "free_y") +
    geom_hline(data = thresh_df, aes(yintercept = threshold), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = paste0(SPECIES, " ", sid, " -- pre-filter QC"), x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

  ggsave(file.path(qc_out_dir, sprintf("QC_Plots_%s.jpeg", sid)),
         p, dpi = 300, width = 3.7 * length(qcMetrics.tmp), height = 4, units = "in")
})

cat("QC plots saved to:", qc_out_dir, "\n")
```

# Filter, remove doublets, save

```{r filter-and-save}
qc_summary <- pmap_dfr(sample_config, function(sample_id, covariate, file, path) {
  obj <- sample.list[[sample_id]]
  total_before <- ncol(obj)

  # Step 1: threshold filter.
  keep <- obj$nFeature_RNA >= qcMetricsThresholds["min_nFeature_RNA"] &
          obj$nFeature_RNA <= qcMetricsThresholds["max_nFeature_RNA"] &
          obj$nCount_RNA   >= qcMetricsThresholds["min_nCount_RNA"] &
          obj$nCount_RNA   <= qcMetricsThresholds["max_nCount_RNA"]
  if (!is.null(MITO_GENES)) keep <- keep & obj$percent_mito <= max_percent_mito
  obj_qc <- subset(obj, cells = colnames(obj)[keep])

  # Step 2: doublets. Run scDblFinder on the ALREADY-FILTERED cells. Its automatic expected doublet
  # rate scales with the number of cells it is given (~1% per 1,000 cells); running it on the raw
  # CellBender output (which still contains many marginal droplets) inflated the Pdam doublet rate
  # to 20-39%. On the filtered cells it was a realistic 6.5-11%.
  sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = GetAssayData(obj_qc, assay = DefaultAssay(obj_qc), layer = "counts"))
  )
  set.seed(SEED)
  sce <- scDblFinder(sce)
  obj_qc$scDblFinder.class <- sce$scDblFinder.class
  obj_qc$scDblFinder.score <- sce$scDblFinder.score

  p_dbl <- ggplot(obj_qc@meta.data, aes(x = scDblFinder.score, fill = scDblFinder.class)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 60, alpha = 0.85, position = "identity") +
    labs(title = paste0(SPECIES, " ", sample_id, " -- scDblFinder score (after threshold filter)"),
         x = "scDblFinder score", y = "cells", fill = "call") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
  ggsave(file.path(qc_out_dir, sprintf("Doublet_Score_%s.jpeg", sample_id)),
         p_dbl, dpi = 300, width = 6, height = 4, units = "in")

  # Step 3: keep singlets.
  cells_keep <- colnames(obj_qc)[obj_qc$scDblFinder.class == "singlet"]
  n_doublets <- ncol(obj_qc) - length(cells_keep)
  obj_filtered <- subset(obj_qc, cells = cells_keep)

  saveRDS(obj_filtered, file.path(qc_rds_dir, sprintf("SeuratObjectFiltered_%s_%s.rds", SPECIES, sample_id)))

  tibble(
    sample_id                   = sample_id,
    covariate                   = covariate,
    total_cells_before          = total_before,
    total_cells_after_qc_filter = ncol(obj_qc),
    n_doublets_removed          = n_doublets,
    pct_doublets                = round(100 * n_doublets / ncol(obj_qc), 2),
    total_cells_kept            = ncol(obj_filtered),
    pct_kept                    = round(100 * ncol(obj_filtered) / total_before, 1),
    median_nFeature             = median(obj_filtered$nFeature_RNA),
    median_nCount               = median(obj_filtered$nCount_RNA),
    median_log10GenesPerUMI     = round(median(obj_filtered$log10GenesPerUMI), 3),
    pct_below_novelty_reference = round(100 * mean(obj_filtered$log10GenesPerUMI < noveltyReferenceThreshold), 1)
  )
})

write_csv(qc_summary, file.path(qc_out_dir, sprintf("QC_Filtered_Summary_%s.csv", SPECIES)))
qc_summary
```

<!--
CHECK BEFORE MOVING ON
- pct_doublets should be roughly 0.5-10% for 10x data. Much higher usually means scDblFinder was
  given too many (unfiltered) cells, not that the data are bad.
- In Doublet_Score_<sample>.jpeg the singlet/doublet boundary ideally sits in a trough. With low-UMI
  data there is often no second peak and the cut falls in the right tail; fine if the rate is sensible.
- Next: scrnaseq_2_ClusterCalling.Rmd reads QC_Files/SeuratObjectFiltered_<SPECIES>_<sample>.rds.
-->
